story_title: NVIDIA Puts Groq 3 LPX in Production, Reaching 3,400 Tokens/Sec for Long-Context AI Agents
why_this_story: NVIDIA officially released production metrics for its Vera Rubin rack-scale architecture with Groq 3 LPX, demonstrating an unprecedented 3,400 tokens/second on 100,000-token long contexts—4x faster than any competing platform.

story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI bottlenecks are about training larger models, but NVIDIA's new LPX architecture proves the new battleground is ultra-low-latency decode speed for autonomous agents.

caption:
NVIDIA just put its Groq 3 LPX inference platform into full production, achieving 3,400 tokens per second on 100,000-token long-context workloads in Gemma 4 31B benchmarks.

As AI shifts from single chat prompts to continuous, multi-agent reasoning, decode latency has become the primary bottleneck. By codesigning Rubin GPUs with up to 256 Groq 3 LP30 LPUs per rack, NVIDIA is aiming to resolve the tradeoff between throughput and response speed.

Key details from the release:
• 4x faster token generation on Gemma 4 31B compared to nearest platforms.
• SpaceXAI adopting Vera CPUs for agentic orchestration from Earth data centers to orbital satellites.
• Cloud providers like Nebius and CoreWeave deploying LPX and Spectrum-X Multiplane to build dedicated 'Token Factories'.
